state.brief: Consider whether canlang should retain its lowercase then body marker or adopt scenario-direct statements. AI authors this business CRUD SaaS language; adoption leads the requirements, with token efficiency, trustworthy generation and simplicity serving it. The requested discussion supplies a candidate rather than proof of its merits. There is no implemented parser/runtime and no tokenizer or agent reliability evaluation. Only this marker is at issue: scenario and uppercase Given/When/Then survive, indentation stays one space, and wide/minimum-line formatting is not reopened.
state.facts: Scenario signatures declare input types and distinguish by user permission from on trusted ingress. A require may be an initial child before then, which either prefixes simple semicolon-delimited statements or opens a deeper block. Those blocks permit bindings, checks, effects, returns, if/else and for structures. Indentation carries lexical depth. Atomic mutations encompass the whole operation, and a failed require rolls back provisional state and delivery intentions irrespective of its position; this behavior does not arise from then. Read operations remain pure with mandatory typed results. Observed sources contain 254 scenarios, each with a marker: 100 inline plus 154 standalone. Within marker-owned blocks, 34 requires appear. Therefore validation can continue after the marker. Descriptions are # metadata and independent BDD observations reside in attached test-only examples.
state.candidate: Under the proposed spelling, executable children belong directly to the scenario and run in written order. For an inline form, strip only the then prefix. For a block form, remove that line and reduce its subtree depth by one, leaving internal conditional/iteration relationships intact. The existing examples keyword identifies an attached test block with no production effects. Migration must keep statement position, dataflow names, permissions, result rules, rollback and authored observations; there is no assumed blanket guarantee of preservation. It may not relocate checks or coalesce separate effects.
state.comparison: The marker-bearing option has an explicit visual/parser delimiter for the body and a container distinct from leading checks and tests. It repeats a keyword 254 times and contributes 154 standalone lines and their deeper subtree indentation, without a semantic promise that validation ends there. The marker-free option can avoid that overhead and place every guard/action in one ordered body. Possible new failure modes are broken branch depth during rewriting, changed diagnostics/parser expectations and test rows entering execution through a poorly specified examples boundary. Existing statement recognition and a reserved test-block rule must be sufficient or be clarified. Neither benefit nor harm has an actual token or generation study here. Both are proposed canonical alternatives, not extra ways of doing CRUD or a directive to combine lines.

examples.existing:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 then
  let selected=item.Part
  require count(selected)>0
  for part in selected limit=100
   require part.ready
   set part {done=true}
  set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done
examples.proposed:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 let selected=item.Part
 require count(selected)>0
 for part in selected limit=100
  require part.ready
  set part {done=true}
 set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done

state.limits: These representative snippets show only the structural rewrite using hypothetical declared types/fixtures. They are not compiled programs or an equivalence proof. Weigh the two alternatives and preserve uncertainty in the yes/no judgment.

remove_then.instructions: Is omission of lowercase then preferable to retaining it for scenario bodies under this proposal, with the stated ordering/test requirements and competing structure risks taken into account?
